<Callout title="Spec v1, rolling out">
  The language is specified in
  [`docs/PLUGIN-LANGUAGE.md`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness/blob/master/docs/PLUGIN-LANGUAGE.md)
  (spec version 1). The marketplace already lists and validates `PLUGIN.md` plugins; the app's
  interpreter and install sheet are landing in the app and the SDK (`@pku-harness/sdk` `lang/`).
  This page summarises the spec. When the two disagree, the spec wins.
</Callout>

A declarative plugin is to PKU Harness what a `SKILL.md` folder is to an agent: **a folder you
can share as a link**. The app reads it and runs its declared steps with a small, safe
interpreter. It never downloads or runs plugin code, so a new plugin or an update needs no app
release and no server.

Use one for anything that is a few campus or public requests plus some extraction: free
classrooms, canteen hours, notices, grades, library reads. Things the language can't express
safely become **host abilities** in the harness, which any plugin can then use. For a server you
run yourself, write a [remote plugin](/docs/build/remote-plugin).

## Layout

```
classrooms/
  PLUGIN.md              # manifest (YAML frontmatter) + instructions for the agent (Markdown)
  tools/free.yaml        # one tool per file (or inline in the frontmatter)
  widgets/overview.json  # dashboard widget: generative-UI spec + bindings
  screens/…json          # full-page generative-UI screens
  tests/free.yaml        # recorded fixtures for the CLI; never fetched by the app
  README.md, assets/     # for humans and the marketplace; ignored by the app
```

- One plugin per folder; a repo can hold many. The marketplace handle is `owner/repo/path`.
- The app only loads files **named in the frontmatter** (relative paths, no `..`), so any static
  host works: GitHub, a gist, your own server.
- UTF-8 text; the files the app loads total at most **512 KB**.

## The manifest

```md title="classrooms/PLUGIN.md"
---
spec: 1
id: classrooms
name: 空闲教室
description: 查询各教学楼今天、明天、后天的空闲教室。
version: 1.2.0
author: pkuinfo
icon: location
network: [portal.pku.edu.cn]
tools:
  free: tools/free.yaml
widgets:
  overview: widgets/overview.json
dataSources:
  overview: { tool: free, args: { day: today }, ttl: 30m }
i18n:
  en: { name: Free classrooms, description: Free classrooms in each teaching building. }
---

Use `free` when the user asks where to study or which rooms are free. Periods are 1–12
(1 = 08:00). Answer with the building and room, and the free period ranges.
```

Required: `spec: 1`, `id`, `name`, `description` (4–200 characters), `version` (semver),
`author`. The declarations that matter most are the ones students see before installing:

| Field | Declares |
|---|---|
| `campus` | Campus services the plugin may call **with the user's session** (`card`, `treehole`, `elective`, `cwfw`, …). The harness signs those requests; the plugin never sees a password, cookie or token. |
| `network` | Public hosts it may call (HTTPS only). |
| `abilities` | Host abilities: `todos`, `timetable`, `scheduler`, `browser`, `campusPage`, `otp`, `sms`, `verify`, `files`, `crypto`. |
| `tools` | Each tool's `effect`: `read`, `write`, `money` or `public`. |

Also available: `dataSources`, `widgets`, `screens`, `settings`, `commands`, `defaultModes`,
`cloud`, `i18n`, and `remote: { mcp, auth }` to describe a remote MCP server with a `PLUGIN.md`.
The field-by-field reference, and what the marketplace checks, is in the
[manifest reference](/docs/marketplace/manifest).

The **Markdown body** is sent to the model as the plugin's instructions. Keep it short: when to
use which tool, and what the numbers mean.

## Tools

A tool is data: a title for users, a description for the model, an honest effect, typed input,
then **steps** that make requests and transform the responses, and a `return` expression.

```yaml title="tools/free.yaml (abridged)"
title: 空闲教室
description: Free rooms in one building (or all) for today, tomorrow or the day after.
effect: read
input:
  building: { type: string, optional: true, description: 'e.g. 二教, 理教' }
  day: { enum: [today, tomorrow, after], default: today }
steps:
  - let: page
    request:
      url: https://portal.pku.edu.cn/publicQuery/ctrl/topic/myTopic/retrClassRoomFree.do
      query: { buildingName: '${input.building}', time: '今天' }
    as: json
return: "page.rows.map(r => ({ room: r.room }))"
```

Steps can request declared hosts or campus services, extract with CSS selectors, JSON paths or
regexes, transform with safe expressions, keep state in the plugin's own storage, and call
declared abilities. There are no unbounded loops, no `eval` and no JavaScript; the interpreter
enforces time, size and operation limits. See the spec for steps, expressions and limits.

## Install links

Students install a plugin by pasting a link in the app (设置 → 插件), scanning a QR code, or
tapping *Open in app* on the [marketplace](/marketplace). The app accepts:

| Form | Example |
|---|---|
| GitHub folder | `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/tree/<ref>/<path>` |
| GitHub repo root | `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` (PLUGIN.md at the root) |
| GitHub file | `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob/<ref>/<path>/PLUGIN.md` |
| Any HTTPS URL of a `PLUGIN.md` | a raw gist URL, your own server |
| Deep link | `pkuharness://plugin?src=<url-encoded link>` |

Before installing, the app validates everything and shows the **permission sheet**: campus
services, hosts, abilities, the effect of each tool, and whether the plugin is verified.
Unverified plugins start with `write`, `money` and `public` tools on *ask*, and their results are
treated as untrusted data.

## Updates

The app re-fetches an installed plugin's link on start (at most daily) and on pull-to-refresh:

- same content hash: nothing happens;
- new content, same declarations: applied, with an "updated to 1.3.0" note;
- wider declarations (a new campus service, host, ability or stronger effect): held until the
  user accepts.

Users can pin a plugin or roll back to the previous version. So publishing an update is just a
`git push`.

## Publish

Push the folder to a public GitHub repo, then submit the repo on the
[marketplace](/marketplace/submit). It finds every `PLUGIN.md`, checks the paths and
declarations, and shows exactly what students will see. See
[Publishing](/docs/marketplace/publishing) and the [review rules](/docs/marketplace/review).
